paper.title: The SIMON and SPECK Families of Lightweight Block Ciphers

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm description; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: Speck64/96, Speck64/128, Speck128/128, Speck128/192 and Speck128/256 encrypt the five appendix plaintexts to the five published ciphertexts (5 of 5 vectors)
decrypting each of those ciphertexts returns the plaintext (5 of 5 round trips)

expected_values_source.what: the five Speck known-answer vectors of the paper's appendix, as transcribed in the Linux kernel crypto self-test file (comment: "taken from the original paper") and in the Crypto++ test-vector file speck.txt; the two transcriptions agree on all 5 (compared programmatically). Both print the vectors byte-reversed relative to the paper's word notation (the kernel comment says the authors confirmed little-endian bytes and (y, x) word order); the program's tables are in the paper's printed word order, obtained by reversing the bytes of each whole string
expected_values_source.note: the paper PDF itself was not fetched (eprint.iacr.org returns 403 here), so the numbers are the paper's as relayed by two public transcriptions; the vectors are data copied as numbers, no code was copied

negative_control: built with SPECK_ALPHA=7 (rotation constant 7 instead of 8), 0 of 5 vectors match and the program exits 1 (the decrypt round trips still pass, 5 of 5, because encryption and decryption stay mutually inverse)
not_checked: the Speck variants with 32-, 48- and 96-bit blocks (no public transcription of their vectors was fetched)
the Simon family (see the simon folder)
security claims, hardware or software performance figures
byte-order conventions other than the one fixed by the vectors
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the five published Speck ciphertexts for their appendix inputs and inverts them. It does not show the cipher is secure.
